# Section 6 - Procedures
## Part A - Amount of OS-HELP Loans
(6)  The OS-HELP Loan amount a student can apply for in a six-month period must be between:
  1. a minimum of AUD $1,000; and
  2. a maximum amount which is indexed annually and published in the OS-HELP Loan application documents available via the [Study Assist website](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=253&version=3&associated).


### Study in Asian Countries
(7)  Students who undertake study in an eligible Asian country may be eligible for a higher value OS-HELP Loan.
(8)  Where such students are offered an OS-HELP Loan they may also be eligible for a supplementary loan to support award or non-award Asian language study where they:
  1. request the supplementary loan when completing their OS-HELP Requisition Form;
  2. provide evidence that: 
    1. they are still enrolled in the Asian language study when making the request;
    2. the provider is external to the University;
    3. the language they are studying is an official language of the country where they are undertaking the overseas study.


(9)  A supplementary loan amount is added to the OS-HELP Loan and does not count towards the lifetime maximum of two (2) OS-HELP Loans per student.
(10)  Students are not eligible for a supplementary loan if their Asian language study is part of their home university course of enrolment.
## Part B - Eligibility for OS-HELP
### General Conditions
(11)  Students applying for an OS-HELP Loan must meet all eligibility requirements of the Department of Education. A student must:
  1. be an Australian citizen, permanent humanitarian visa holder, eligible former permanent humanitarian visa holder, Pacific Engagement Visa (PEV) holder or a New Zealand Special Visa (SCV) holder, or eligible former New Zealand SCV holder who meets the residency requirements and who will be resident in Australia at the time of applying;
  2. not have received OS-HELP on more than one other occasion and not within the same six-month period by La Trobe or any other provider;
  3. be enrolled in an undergraduate or postgraduate course of study at La Trobe as a Commonwealth-Supported student;
  4. have already completed at least one equivalent full-time student load (EFTSL) of study, or the equivalent of one EFTSL (minimum of 120 credit points), that counts towards their course of study (any credit granted from a previous degree or external qualification must have been completed in a Commonwealth-Supported Place (CSP) to count towards the completed Equivalent Full-Time Study Load (EFSTL) requirement of 120 credit points);
  5. during their program be undertaking full-time study with an approved overseas higher education institution or other recognised organisation;
  6. have their overseas study count as credit, or be a course requirement, for the course of study that they are enrolled in at La Trobe;
  7. still have at least 0.125 EFTSL (15 credit points) of study yet to complete in their course of study on return from their overseas study;
  8. meet the Australian Taxation Office Tax File Number (TFN) requirements and provide a Unique Student Identifier (USI);
  9. be approved by Learning Abroad to participate in the relevant program;
  10. not have already completed the overseas study for which OS HELP is being sought, regardless of whether the student is still overseas or has returned to Australia.


(12)  Students are entitled to a maximum of two (2) OS-HELP Loans in their lifetime.
(13)  OS-HELP Loans are allocated for a six-month period from the date of commencement of the overseas study, regardless of the duration of the overseas study.
(14)  OS-HELP is not available for students undertaking their whole course outside Australia; however students may be outside Australia when submitting an application.
### Determining Eligibility for Short-Term Programs
(15)  In order to confirm eligibility for Short-Term Programs, a full-time load is calculated by using a formula that takes account of the credit points that will be achieved, and the duration of the program (see [Study Abroad webpage](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=269&version=3&associated)).
## Part C - Applying For an OS-HELP Loan
### Prior Required Approvals
(16)  Prior to submitting an application for an OS-HELP Loan, students must obtain a number of approvals and accompanying evidence:
  1. confirmation that their proposed overseas Exchange or Short-Term Program has been approved for credit, or is a course requirement, for their course of enrolment at La Trobe;
  2. evidence that allows the La Trobe OS-HELP team to confirm that the study will be undertaken on a full-time basis (see the [Study Abroad webpage](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=269&version=3&associated) for guidance);
  3. acceptance by the host university or provider into the overseas program;
  4. La Trobe Learning Abroad acceptance notification.


(17)  Applications for OS-HELP Loans for approved overseas study can be submitted at any time from six (6) months prior to the start date of their overseas program, but no earlier. Where students intending to participate in an Exchange program have all the necessary documentation and approvals, it is recommended that they submit their application no later than:
  1. 1 May for an Exchange commencing between 1 July and 31 December of that year;
  2. 1 November for an Exchange commencing between 1 January and 30 June of the next year.


(18)  Students must disclose if they have been a previous recipient of an OS-HELP Loan.
(19)  Students may apply for two (2) consecutive six-month periods of overseas study at the same time; however any second six-month loan offer and payment will be conditional on the student remaining eligible at the commencement of the second period.
## Part D - Approval, Acceptance and Payment
(20)  Student Administration assesses applications for eligibility in accordance with the Department of Education eligibility criteria. Where there are more applications than available loans preference may be given to students who:
  1. have a higher Weighted Average Mark (WAM) at the time the application is submitted;
  2. are participating in a semester-length overseas study program;
  3. have not previously received OS HELP;
  4. can demonstrate financial hardship and/or educational disadvantage.


(21)  Students will normally be notified of their eligibility for an OS-HELP Loan within 20 business days of submitting their application, where:
  1. the application is submitted within the allowable timeframe (that is six [6] months prior to their overseas program start date and prior to completing the program);
  2. all relevant documentation and evidence is available (such as results where applicable).


(22)  Notification letters will confirm the amount of the approved OS-HELP Loan in Australian dollars and include the rights and responsibilities of the student in relation to the loan.
(23)  When accepting their offer students must:
  1. complete an OS-HELP Electronic Commonwealth Assistance Form (eCAF) via StudentOnLine;
  2. complete the submission of all required information via the Government portal;
  3. return the OS-HELP Requisition Form and Acceptance (OS-HELP Debt Confirmation) Form to Student Administration.


(24)  Payments are processed to students’ nominated bank accounts within 10 business days of all required documents being received.
(25)  If a student has been offered two consecutive OS-HELP Loans the second payment can only be made six months after the first payment.
## Part E - Variations to Loans
### Unpaid OS-Help Loans
(26)  Students are permitted to reduce the loan amount offered provided the request is received before they submit the eCAF and OS-HELP Requisition and Acceptance Form. Students may be required to submit a new OS-HELP application in these circumstances.
(27)  The University will withdraw a loan offer as soon as practicable before it has been paid to the student’s bank account where:
  1. the student’s circumstances change so that they no longer meet the eligibility criteria
  2. it is determined the student has provided false or misleading information
  3. the student will not be undertaking the overseas study.


(28)  Where an unpaid offer is withdrawn the University will notify the student in writing.
### Paid OS-HELP Loans
(29)  OS-HELP Loans that have already been paid cannot be remitted by the University under any circumstances. Once a loan has been paid to the student account the debt is included in the student’s accumulated HELP debt and may only be repaid through the Australian taxation system. The University is not required to take any action where a student has been paid their OS-HELP loan:
  1. and does not proceed with their overseas study; or
  2. their circumstances change in such a way that a provider determines that the student no longer meets the OS-HELP eligibility criteria.


## Part F - Confirmation of Liability
(30)  The University must issue a Commonwealth Assistance Notice (CAN) within 28 days of the date on which the OS-HELP debt was incurred. A student is taken to have incurred their OS-HELP debt on the day the provider makes the OS-HELP payment to the student.
(31)  When a student believes the information on the CAN is incorrect, the student may, within 14 calendar days of the CAN being issued, request a correction. This request may be made electronically. The student’s request should specify which information the student considers is incorrect and the reasons why they consider it to be incorrect. Making the request does not affect the student’s liability to pay the tuition fee, or the student’s HELP eligibility.
## Part G - False and Misleading Information
(32)  Where a student in receipt of an OS-HELP loan is suspected to have provided false or misleading information the University is required to notify the Department of Education and provide the Department with a copy of the student’s application and any other relevant information or material the Department requests. The student will be subject to proceedings under the University’s [General Misconduct Statute 2009](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/directory/summary.php?legislation=37).
## Part H - Review
(33)  Students may seek a review of decisions made under this Policy where they are of the view that this Policy has not been correctly applied. A request to review a decision made under this Procedure must be lodged within 10 business days of the relevant process or decision by replying in writing to the original notification or statement, and addressing the request to the Director, Academic Services.
(34)  The Director, Academic Services will arrange for a review of the decision by a senior staff member who was not involved in the original decision.
(35)  A written outcome will be provided within 10 business days of the date the request was received by the University.
(36)  A request to review the decision may be dismissed where the applicant cannot substantiate their request in line with the allowable grounds.
### Further Review
(37)  Where a student is not satisfied with the outcome of any review they may apply to the University Ombudsman for a further review of the matter, in accordance with the University’s Statutes and Regulations.
(38)  If a student is not satisfied with the outcome of the review of the University Ombudsman, they may lodge a complaint with the [National Student Ombudsman](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=462&version=1&associated).
[Top of Page](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=204#document-top)
# Section 7 - Definitions
(39)  For the purposes of this Policy:
  1. overseas study: study undertaken outside of Australia that counts towards the requirements of the course of study in which the student is enrolled with their home provider.

[Top of Page](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=204#document-top)
# Section 8 - Authority and Associated Information
(40)  This Policy is made under the [La Trobe University Act 2009](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/directory/summary.php?legislation=8).
(41)  Associated information for this Policy includes:
  1. [Study Assist website](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=253&version=3&associated)
  2. [OS-HELP Guidelines](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=471&version=3&associated)
  3. La Trobe [Study Abroad - Costs and Funding](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=269&version=3&associated) webpage

sections.heading: Section 2 - Purpose
sections.text:
(1)  This Policy informs prospective applicants, Deans, and Outside Studies Programs Committees, of the principles associated with the Outside Studies Program (OSP).
[Top of Page](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=82#document-top)

sections.heading: Section 3 - Scope
sections.text:
(2)  This Policy applies to:
  1. all Campuses;
  2. all post probation academic staff members on continuing contracts (teaching and research, teaching focused or research continuing), employed full time and part time (0.5 FTE and above).

[Top of Page](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=82#document-top)

sections.heading: Section 4 - Key Decisions
sections.text:
| Key Decisions  |  Role  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Approve OSP applications via recommendations from the OSP Committee.  | Provost  |  
| Assess and approve OSP applications for academic staff who work in a central area rather than a school.  | Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Innovation)  |  
[Top of Page](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=82#document-top)

sections.heading: Section 5 - Policy Statement
sections.text:
(3)  The purpose of an Outside Studies Program (OSP) is to promote research and scholarship. This period free from the full range of University duties provides an opportunity for academic staff to focus on research and scholarship, including exposure to and collaboration with field-leading scholars and industry partners.
(4)  Normally staff will pursue their programs at major centres of learning overseas although industry based programs may be undertaken in Australia or overseas.
(5)  OSP is an important step in the development of academics. Deans will take appropriate note of this when determining the capacity of the School to cover workloads. Academic staff have a responsibility to establish a long-term research/scholarship development plan with their supervisor, including a plan for OSP.
(6)  La Trobe is committed to ensuring that the OSP application process is fair and equitable, taking family and other responsibilities into consideration.
[Top of Page](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=82#document-top)

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.text:
(7)  OSP is not an automatic entitlement. Approval to undertake a program should not be assumed even when the applicant satisfies the basic eligibility requirements.
(8)  All post probation academic staff members on continuing contracts (teaching and research, teaching focussed or research continuing), employed full time and part time, 0.5 EFT (50% of full time) and above, are eligible to apply for OSP.
(9)  Fixed term contract staff are not entitled to apply for OSP, unless provided for under the [La Trobe University Enterprise Agreement 2023](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=422&version=2&associated) as amended from time to time.
(10)  Staff must normally have worked at La Trobe in a continuing role and must have accumulated at least three years of service by January 1 in the year in which they submit an application for OSP, unless prior service as an academic staff member at another higher education institution has been recognised, in which case staff must normally have served and accumulated two years at La Trobe by January 1 in the year in which they apply for OSP (see 'Recognition of Prior Service' below).
(11)  Should an application be made by a staff member who has not served three years at La Trobe it must be accompanied by a justification from the Dean indicating the special circumstances, or a copy of the contract of employment confirming prior approval to submit an early application.
(12)  OSP will not normally be used to undertake PhD work as this can be accommodated under alternative workload arrangements.

sections.heading: Payment of Salary
sections.text: (13)  The University will continue to pay a staff member’s salary during their period of OSP.

sections.heading: OSP Accumulation
sections.text:
(14)  Eligible academic staff members may apply for OSP after three years of continuous service, from commencement at La Trobe or from the end of the last period of OSP.
(15)  The period of OSP available accumulates at the rate of one month (full time) for each six months of full time service, with a maximum accumulation of twelve months. For part time staff the period of OSP available accumulates using their average part time fraction over the period of service. See [OSP How-to Guide](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=233&version=2&associated) for further information.
(16)  A staff member may apply for an OSP of shorter duration than the period of OSP accumulated. The balance of the accumulated OSP, to a maximum of 6 months, will be carried over and may be used towards a future program.
(17)  Any period of paid leave shall count in assessing the OSP accumulated.

sections.heading: Recognition of Prior Service for the purposes of OSP
sections.text:
(18)  The University recognises prior service as an academic staff member of other Australian universities and higher education providers.
(19)  Academic staff shall be able to apply for recognition of a maximum of three years of prior continuous service in a full time or part time (0.5 FTE and above) position, dependent upon such service being confirmed by the other university.
(20)  Provided there is not more than two months between the cessation of employment with another university and commencement at La Trobe, continuity shall be deemed not to have been broken. The period between cessation and commencement will not be taken into account in determining the period of service.
(21)  While staff on fixed term contracts are not eligible to apply for OSP, a staff member who is appointed to a continuing position following a fixed term appointment may apply for recognition of prior service, for the purpose of OSP, for the period of the fixed term appointment.
(22)  For staff seeking recognition of prior service for a fixed term appointment at La Trobe, approval to undertake OSP will not normally be granted until a minimum of two years has been served in a continuing position.
(23)  Staff wishing to apply for recognition of prior service for the purposes of OSP should provide relevant details to their Supervisor and the School OSP Contact before submitting an application. The details will be verified with People & Culture.

sections.heading: Requirement to Return to the Service of the University
sections.text:
(24)  Normally eligible staff may apply for OSP provided that they undertake, and are eligible, to return to the service of the University for a period at least equal to the length of the program.
(25)  Staff who do not comply with the requirement to return to the service of the University as defined above may be required to reimburse the University the financial grant provided. The amount repayable will be determined on the basis of the period of service to the University after completion of the OSP.

sections.heading: Location of Program
sections.text: (26)  Normally, applicants will pursue their programs at major centres of learning overseas, except for industry based programs which may be undertaken in Australia or overseas. It is recognised that some research or teaching focused programs will be more appropriately carried out in Australia. In some circumstances programs can be taken at La Trobe. Where a program is to be taken in Australia, a case must be made explaining why this is appropriate and an affiliation with a local university, major centre of learning or equivalent institution arranged.

sections.heading: Length of Program
sections.text:
(27)  Programs will normally be for a period between three months and six months, however applications for programs of less than three months, or greater than six months but less than 12 months, will be considered.
(28)  Only in exceptional circumstances will an OSP be approved for a duration in excess of the period of OSP accumulated.

sections.heading: Timing of Program
sections.text:
(29)  The timing of a program shall be such that, in the opinion of the Dean and the OSP Committee, it will cause the least disruption to the academic needs of the School. Deans are required to provide a clear indication on this matter on the application form.
(30)  It is normally expected that:
  1. a program may extend for up to six months;
  2. the time interval between OSPs will be at least three years by January 1 in the year in which a subsequent OSP application is submitted.

sections.heading: Recreation and Long Service Leave
sections.text: (31)  An applicant will be required to incorporate in the application at least the amount of recreation leave that will accrue during the OSP. Applicants whose programs include recreation or long service leave will not conduct their studies during such leave. Leave is to be defined prior to commencement of the program and amended only with approval from the Dean.

sections.heading: Absences Not Classified as Part of an OSP
Criteria
Consideration of Applications
How to lodge an Application
sections.text:
(42)  Prior to preparing an application intending applicants should consult with their Dean to determine the feasibility of submitting an application at this time. The Dean will provide preliminary advice to the applicant in light of the operational needs of the School and the individual’s development goals and career stage.
(43)  Applications will be called once each year, normally in March, for programs to commence in the following year. Applications will be considered and evaluated on a competitive basis.
(44)  In exceptional circumstances consideration may be given to an application received out of session.
(45)  To lodge an application:
  1. applicants must complete the OSP Application form available on the [OSP intranet](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=233&version=2&associated);
  2. the applicant's line supervisor will seek agreement from appropriate replacement supervisors and/or subject coordinators to cover their workload;
  3. applications must be endorsed with comments and a recommendation by the Dean (who will consult with the supervisor and/or senior academics of the discipline regarding the merit of the proposed program); and
  4. applications without the endorsement of the Dean are not to be submitted to the OSP Committee.


(46)  The Dean's recommendation for endorsement will attest that:
  1. the applicant’s workload can be covered;
  2. HDR supervision can be covered by an appropriate alternative supervisor who has agreed to provide supervision; and
  3. outcomes of any previous OSPs have been considered in assessing the current application. 


(47)  The applicant sights the comments of the Dean and has the opportunity to make further comment. The applicant then submits the endorsed application to the OSP Committee via the School OSP contact.
(48)  The Outside Studies Programs Committee's recommendation for approval and the Provost's approval for a program may be withdrawn if subsequent events mean that resources are not available to cover the period of OSP.

sections.heading: Report on a Completed OSP
sections.text:
(49)  Within two months of return from an OSP the staff member is required to present a report through the Dean to the OSP Chair. After consultation with the staff member, the Dean will provide an assessment and evaluation of the success of the program in meeting the original objectives.
(50)  Reports will be scrutinised closely by the OSP Committee Chair to ensure that the objectives of the program have been achieved.
(51)  Unless exceptional circumstances intervene, failure to submit a satisfactory report may result in the OSP Chair deciding that a future application for an OSP not be considered for a specific period of time and/or a refund of all or part of the financial grant be made by the staff member.
(52)  Following return from an OSP the staff member will normally present a seminar in the school on the research completed during the OSP, as part of the expected dissemination of outcomes described under 'Criteria' above.

sections.heading: Guidelines on Preparation of Report
Part C - Outside Studies Programs Committee
sections.text:
(56)  There will be an OSP Committee to consider applications for OSP. Membership of the OSP Committee will comprise:
  1. Provost or nominee (Chair)
  2. Deans
  3. Deputy Provost or nominee


(57)  Gender balance must be maintained wherever possible.
(58)  Other members, such as immediate past Chairs of OSP Committees, may be co-opted onto committees for their expertise.
(59)  In attendance, but not voting:
  1. Administrative officer (secretariat)
  2. Executive Director, Operations or nominee (adviser).


(60)  The role of the Outside Studies Programs Committee will be to:
  1. consider applications from the Schools;
  2. provide recommendations to the Provost to approve applications;
  3. scrutinise and provide feedback on reports on completed OSPs;
  4. oversee and consider matters relating to OSP including the development of rules and standards relating to OSP.

sections.heading: Approval for Overseas Travel
sections.text:
(61)  Approval for an OSP which includes a component of overseas travel is contingent upon University approval to travel to the destinations listed in the application.
(62)  Travel to places where a DFAT warning against travel is in place will not be approved unless a convincing reason is provided to indicate that the travel is essential.
(63)  Applicants whose OSP includes overseas travel should refer to the [OSP How-to Guide](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=233&version=2&associated) and the University's Guide on [Booking and managing travel](https://intranet.latrobe.edu.au/tasks-and-processes/travel-transport-and-parking).

sections.heading: Financial Assistance
Financial Grant
sections.text:
(65)  For staff members travelling overseas, interstate or intrastate on OSP, a grant may be payable to assist with expenses. The amount of the grant is the same for full time and part time staff members. For overseas and interstate travel it is based on the length of time to be spent overseas/interstate, with a minimum component of one month. Staff members who receive an overseas grant will not be eligible for an interstate or intrastate grant.
(66)  In addition to the grant payable to staff travelling overseas an allowance for up to three dependents will be paid, subject to evidence that they are travelling with the staff member.
(67)  Financial grants apply only to the period of OSP and not to any long service leave, excess recreation leave or leave without pay taken in conjunction with an OSP.
(68)  For further information on financial grants, including amounts payable, please refer to the [OSP How-to Guide](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=233&version=2&associated).

sections.heading: Salary Advance
sections.text:
(69)  A staff member may claim half their normal salary for the period of overseas study in the form of a salary advance for travel purposes, subject to Australian Taxation Office rules. Refer to the [OSP How-to Guide](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=233&version=2&associated) for further information.
(70)  An alternative mechanism for a salary advance is provided in the [La Trobe University Enterprise Agreement 2023](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=422&version=2&associated); with four weeks’ notice, a staff member will be entitled to payment in advance for periods of paid OSP in excess of two (2) weeks up to a maximum of 12 weeks. Enquiries may be directed to People & Culture.

sections.heading: Part E - Variations to Programs
sections.text:
(71)  Variations to approved programs must be submitted to the OSP administrator in advance.
(72)  The University's online travel booking and leave request systems must not be used to alter a previously approved OSP and associated recreation leave or long service leave.
(73)  Where a staff member requests a postponement of the commencement date for a period not exceeding six months from the commencement date of the approved OSP, and this is approved by the Dean, no further approval will be required.
(74)  Where a postponement is for a period greater than six months from the commencement date of the approved OSP, the staff member must resubmit the application.
(75)  Where a staff member requests a substantial change to a program, full details of the changes must be submitted for the approval of the OSP Chair, through the Dean. Any change which involves the elimination of an overseas component will be automatically regarded as a substantial change.
(76)  Where the Dean or OSP Chair considers that a changed program is of insufficient merit, approval for all or part of the program may be withdrawn by the OSP Committee on the recommendation of the OSP Chair.
(77)  Variations to approved programs involving an extension to, or addition of, an overseas or interstate component may be approved, but normally no further grant will be provided.

sections.heading: Part F - Unsuccessful Applications
sections.text:
(78)  The decision not to approve an application will be based on the quality/merit of the proposed program and/or on the resources available within the School.
(79)  The OSP Chair will provide unsuccessful applicants with brief written advice outlining the reasons why their applications were not approved.
(80)  Where the decision was based on the quality/merit of the proposed program the letter will include advice on areas that would need to be strengthened before a future application was submitted. The OSP Chair is encouraged to meet with the applicants individually to discuss this further.
(81)  It is suggested that applicants use this advice, in consultation with their supervisor, when revising their workload and performance development plans.

sections.heading: Appeals
sections.text:
(82)  Applicants will have the right to appeal against the decision in relation to their applications. Appeals can only be made on the grounds that the procedures outlined in this document were not followed by the OSP Committee in reaching its decision.
(83)  An appeal is to be lodged with the Provost via email to OSPC@latrobe.edu.au within one month of the applicant’s receipt of advice on the outcome of the application.
(84)  Any appeal against the decision made by the Provost in relation to an appeal should be made to the University Ombudsman and only on the grounds of failure to follow the procedures pertaining to the submission and consideration of an appeal.

sections.heading: Part G - Authorities/Delegations
sections.text:
(85)  The OSP Chair is responsible for: 
  1. overseeing the number of programs a school could offer in any one year;
  2. approving programs, with the advice of Deans in consultation with the professor(s) of discipline.


(86)  Reports on completed OSPs:
  1. The OSP Committee will scrutinise and approve reports through the Dean and OSP Chair.

sections.heading: Section 7 - Definitions
sections.text:
(87)  For the purpose of this Policy and Procedure:
  1. Relative to opportunity: relates to acknowledgement of what a staff member can and has achieved given the workload allocation and opportunities available. Personal circumstances that could affect opportunity may include family responsibilities, a temporary or permanent disability, and periods of part-time work and/or absences due to ill-health or injury.

[Top of Page](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=82#document-top)

sections.text:
(88)  This Policy is made under the [La Trobe University Act 2009](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/directory/summary.php?legislation=8).
(89)  Associated information includes:
  1. [Achievement Relative to Opportunity Guidelines](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=478&version=1&associated)

# Section 1 - Key Information

# Section 2 - Purpose
(1)  This Policy informs prospective applicants, Deans, and Outside Studies Programs Committees, of the principles associated with the Outside Studies Program (OSP).
[Top of Page](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=82#document-top)
# Section 3 - Scope
(2)  This Policy applies to:
  1. all Campuses;
  2. all post probation academic staff members on continuing contracts (teaching and research, teaching focused or research continuing), employed full time and part time (0.5 FTE and above).

[Top of Page](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=82#document-top)
# Section 4 - Key Decisions  
| Key Decisions  |  Role  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Approve OSP applications via recommendations from the OSP Committee.  | Provost  |  
| Assess and approve OSP applications for academic staff who work in a central area rather than a school.  | Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Innovation)  |  
[Top of Page](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=82#document-top)
# Section 5 - Policy Statement
(3)  The purpose of an Outside Studies Program (OSP) is to promote research and scholarship. This period free from the full range of University duties provides an opportunity for academic staff to focus on research and scholarship, including exposure to and collaboration with field-leading scholars and industry partners.
(4)  Normally staff will pursue their programs at major centres of learning overseas although industry based programs may be undertaken in Australia or overseas.
(5)  OSP is an important step in the development of academics. Deans will take appropriate note of this when determining the capacity of the School to cover workloads. Academic staff have a responsibility to establish a long-term research/scholarship development plan with their supervisor, including a plan for OSP.
(6)  La Trobe is committed to ensuring that the OSP application process is fair and equitable, taking family and other responsibilities into consideration.
[Top of Page](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=82#document-top)
# Section 6 - Procedures
## Part A - Eligibility and Conditions of Leave
### Eligibility
(7)  OSP is not an automatic entitlement. Approval to undertake a program should not be assumed even when the applicant satisfies the basic eligibility requirements.
(8)  All post probation academic staff members on continuing contracts (teaching and research, teaching focussed or research continuing), employed full time and part time, 0.5 EFT (50% of full time) and above, are eligible to apply for OSP.
(9)  Fixed term contract staff are not entitled to apply for OSP, unless provided for under the [La Trobe University Enterprise Agreement 2023](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=422&version=2&associated) as amended from time to time.
(10)  Staff must normally have worked at La Trobe in a continuing role and must have accumulated at least three years of service by January 1 in the year in which they submit an application for OSP, unless prior service as an academic staff member at another higher education institution has been recognised, in which case staff must normally have served and accumulated two years at La Trobe by January 1 in the year in which they apply for OSP (see 'Recognition of Prior Service' below).
(11)  Should an application be made by a staff member who has not served three years at La Trobe it must be accompanied by a justification from the Dean indicating the special circumstances, or a copy of the contract of employment confirming prior approval to submit an early application.
(12)  OSP will not normally be used to undertake PhD work as this can be accommodated under alternative workload arrangements.
### Payment of Salary
(13)  The University will continue to pay a staff member’s salary during their period of OSP.
### OSP Accumulation
(14)  Eligible academic staff members may apply for OSP after three years of continuous service, from commencement at La Trobe or from the end of the last period of OSP.
(15)  The period of OSP available accumulates at the rate of one month (full time) for each six months of full time service, with a maximum accumulation of twelve months. For part time staff the period of OSP available accumulates using their average part time fraction over the period of service. See [OSP How-to Guide](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=233&version=2&associated) for further information.
(16)  A staff member may apply for an OSP of shorter duration than the period of OSP accumulated. The balance of the accumulated OSP, to a maximum of 6 months, will be carried over and may be used towards a future program.
(17)  Any period of paid leave shall count in assessing the OSP accumulated.
### Recognition of Prior Service for the purposes of OSP
(18)  The University recognises prior service as an academic staff member of other Australian universities and higher education providers.
(19)  Academic staff shall be able to apply for recognition of a maximum of three years of prior continuous service in a full time or part time (0.5 FTE and above) position, dependent upon such service being confirmed by the other university.
(20)  Provided there is not more than two months between the cessation of employment with another university and commencement at La Trobe, continuity shall be deemed not to have been broken. The period between cessation and commencement will not be taken into account in determining the period of service.
(21)  While staff on fixed term contracts are not eligible to apply for OSP, a staff member who is appointed to a continuing position following a fixed term appointment may apply for recognition of prior service, for the purpose of OSP, for the period of the fixed term appointment.
(22)  For staff seeking recognition of prior service for a fixed term appointment at La Trobe, approval to undertake OSP will not normally be granted until a minimum of two years has been served in a continuing position.
(23)  Staff wishing to apply for recognition of prior service for the purposes of OSP should provide relevant details to their Supervisor and the School OSP Contact before submitting an application. The details will be verified with People & Culture.
### Requirement to Return to the Service of the University
(24)  Normally eligible staff may apply for OSP provided that they undertake, and are eligible, to return to the service of the University for a period at least equal to the length of the program.
(25)  Staff who do not comply with the requirement to return to the service of the University as defined above may be required to reimburse the University the financial grant provided. The amount repayable will be determined on the basis of the period of service to the University after completion of the OSP.
### Location of Program
(26)  Normally, applicants will pursue their programs at major centres of learning overseas, except for industry based programs which may be undertaken in Australia or overseas. It is recognised that some research or teaching focused programs will be more appropriately carried out in Australia. In some circumstances programs can be taken at La Trobe. Where a program is to be taken in Australia, a case must be made explaining why this is appropriate and an affiliation with a local university, major centre of learning or equivalent institution arranged.
### Length of Program
(27)  Programs will normally be for a period between three months and six months, however applications for programs of less than three months, or greater than six months but less than 12 months, will be considered.
(28)  Only in exceptional circumstances will an OSP be approved for a duration in excess of the period of OSP accumulated.
### Timing of Program
(29)  The timing of a program shall be such that, in the opinion of the Dean and the OSP Committee, it will cause the least disruption to the academic needs of the School. Deans are required to provide a clear indication on this matter on the application form.
(30)  It is normally expected that:
  1. a program may extend for up to six months;
  2. the time interval between OSPs will be at least three years by January 1 in the year in which a subsequent OSP application is submitted.


### Recreation and Long Service Leave
(31)  An applicant will be required to incorporate in the application at least the amount of recreation leave that will accrue during the OSP. Applicants whose programs include recreation or long service leave will not conduct their studies during such leave. Leave is to be defined prior to commencement of the program and amended only with approval from the Dean.
### Absences Not Classified as Part of an OSP
(32)  Absences from the University which will not be classified as part of an OSP may include:
  1. conferences of less than two weeks duration;
  2. secondment to other institutions;
  3. representing the University elsewhere;
  4. obligations arising from membership of government bodies or international organisations;
  5. exchange of staff between institutions;
  6. other specific purposes such as field work, recommended for approval by the Dean and approved by the OSP Chair. However, in cases where leave to undertake field work was sought in the same year as an OSP the field work would not automatically be considered to be separate from the OSP;
  7. a period of specific training to fit a staff member for a change in task or an upgrading of that task, or to learn the application of a new technique;
  8. long service leave;
  9. recreation leave, except as detailed above.


## Part B - Application Process
### Criteria
(33)  A research focused OSP application must outline a fully developed program with clear objectives to achieve specific outcomes not possible without a period of OSP, that align with the research priorities set out in the University's Strategic Plan and contribute to the University’s research profile. Evidence of how the period of OSP will contribute to the following tangible outcomes within a definable period must be included, including their impact and how they will be disseminated:
  1. publications or non-traditional research outputs in high quality outlets as measured by the relevant disciplines and external measures of quality;
  2. new/external research grant applications with collaborators from host institution/s;
  3. strong international research collaborations or research student and staffing exchanges.


(34)  A teaching focused OSP application must outline a fully developed program with clear objectives that align with University priorities, contribute to the University’s research profile and engage explicitly with the scholarship of learning and teaching. Evidence of how the period of OSP will contribute to the following tangible outcomes within a definable period must be included, including their impact and how they will be disseminated:
  1. publications or non-traditional research outputs in high quality outlets for higher education research;
  2. national or international grant applications related to educational research or innovation with collaborators from host institution/s;
  3. strong national or international teaching or curriculum collaborations or exchanges, along with dissemination of the outcomes of those collaborations.


(35)  An industry focused OSP application must outline a fully developed program, with clear objectives to achieve outcomes not possible without a period of OSP, that align with the industry partnership priorities set out in the University's Strategic Plan and contribute to the University’s partnership profile. Evidence of how the period of OSP will contribute to the following tangible outcomes within a definable period must be included, including their impact and how they will be disseminated:
  1. publications or non-traditional research outputs in high quality outlets as measured by the relevant disciplines and external measures of quality;
  2. new external industry collaborations and new research funding with industry collaborators;
  3. new/external research grant applications with collaborators from host organisation/s;
  4. strong student and staffing exchanges to industry.


### Consideration of Applications
(36)  Applications for OSP from each School are reviewed by the OSP Committee which makes recommendations for approval to the Provost.
(37)  In cases where the OSP Committee cannot recommend for approval all applications that have met the criteria, the following factors will be considered:
  1. early career researchers who are submitting their first OSP applications;
  2. staff who have a very strong record of scholarly or teaching activity.


(38)  The Provost will consider the following prior to approving the recommendations from the Outside Studies Programs Committee:
  1. objectives and academic content of the proposed program will benefit the staff member in terms of research and scholarly activity and provide significant benefit, including improvements in research and/or teaching for the University;
  2. applicant has a workload plan that has scheduled OSP for this period and has met the required measurable goals to be achieved before applying for OSP, with such goals to be relative to opportunity;
  3. proposed program, full details of which are to be provided, justifies the period requested;
  4. applicant’s teaching and other duties can be covered without unreasonable additional duties for other academic staff from the School – such details are to be confirmed by the Dean;
  5. timing of leave causes minimum disruption to the School; and
  6. appropriate recreation leave is included in the period designated as OSP.


(39)  Applications submitted by academic staff who work in a central area of the University, rather than a School, will be assessed and approved by the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Innovation), with input from the Chair of the OSP Committee.
(40)  An applicant for OSP is expected to submit their best and most complete application by the due date. The OSP Committee will have the discretion to request additional information from applicants in cases where there are minor aspects requiring clarification, but not for major revisions.
(41)  Applications which are submitted in an incomplete state, or lacking sufficient details, will not be open to re-submission. Late applications will not be accepted.
### How to lodge an Application
(42)  Prior to preparing an application intending applicants should consult with their Dean to determine the feasibility of submitting an application at this time. The Dean will provide preliminary advice to the applicant in light of the operational needs of the School and the individual’s development goals and career stage.
(43)  Applications will be called once each year, normally in March, for programs to commence in the following year. Applications will be considered and evaluated on a competitive basis.
(44)  In exceptional circumstances consideration may be given to an application received out of session.
(45)  To lodge an application:
  1. applicants must complete the OSP Application form available on the [OSP intranet](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=233&version=2&associated);
  2. the applicant's line supervisor will seek agreement from appropriate replacement supervisors and/or subject coordinators to cover their workload;
  3. applications must be endorsed with comments and a recommendation by the Dean (who will consult with the supervisor and/or senior academics of the discipline regarding the merit of the proposed program); and
  4. applications without the endorsement of the Dean are not to be submitted to the OSP Committee.


(46)  The Dean's recommendation for endorsement will attest that:
  1. the applicant’s workload can be covered;
  2. HDR supervision can be covered by an appropriate alternative supervisor who has agreed to provide supervision; and
  3. outcomes of any previous OSPs have been considered in assessing the current application. 


(47)  The applicant sights the comments of the Dean and has the opportunity to make further comment. The applicant then submits the endorsed application to the OSP Committee via the School OSP contact.
(48)  The Outside Studies Programs Committee's recommendation for approval and the Provost's approval for a program may be withdrawn if subsequent events mean that resources are not available to cover the period of OSP.
### Report on a Completed OSP
(49)  Within two months of return from an OSP the staff member is required to present a report through the Dean to the OSP Chair. After consultation with the staff member, the Dean will provide an assessment and evaluation of the success of the program in meeting the original objectives.
(50)  Reports will be scrutinised closely by the OSP Committee Chair to ensure that the objectives of the program have been achieved.
(51)  Unless exceptional circumstances intervene, failure to submit a satisfactory report may result in the OSP Chair deciding that a future application for an OSP not be considered for a specific period of time and/or a refund of all or part of the financial grant be made by the staff member.
(52)  Following return from an OSP the staff member will normally present a seminar in the school on the research completed during the OSP, as part of the expected dissemination of outcomes described under 'Criteria' above.
#### Guidelines on Preparation of Report
(53)  The report on a completed OSP will include the following:
  1. a brief statement of the purpose of the approved program. Where objectives were not achieved or a marked variation occurred to the approved program, reasons are to be included in the report;
  2. a description of the actual research and other academic activities undertaken is to be detailed under the following headings: 
    1. Nature of research or teaching-focused activities undertaken;
    2. Nature and extent of discussions held with learned colleagues, who are to be named;
    3. Universities or institutions at which research or other work was undertaken, including the names of specific departments;
    4. Attendance at seminars or conferences, and presentation of papers;
    5. Any teaching assignments undertaken;
    6. Any courses undertaken;
    7. Periods spent in each city or country visited;
    8. The status of any written work arising from the program, even if that work was part of a larger project. Written work will be designated ‘in preparation’, ‘submitted’, ‘forthcoming’ or ‘published’.


(54)  The staff member is to assess, where practicable, the degree to which the program has assisted research, teaching or other academic interests and the extent to which it was of benefit to the individual and to the University.
(55)  The staff member is also free to comment on other matters, not necessarily related to their field of work, that are of value to the University.
## Part C - Outside Studies Programs Committee
(56)  There will be an OSP Committee to consider applications for OSP. Membership of the OSP Committee will comprise:
  1. Provost or nominee (Chair)
  2. Deans
  3. Deputy Provost or nominee


(57)  Gender balance must be maintained wherever possible.
(58)  Other members, such as immediate past Chairs of OSP Committees, may be co-opted onto committees for their expertise.
(59)  In attendance, but not voting:
  1. Administrative officer (secretariat)
  2. Executive Director, Operations or nominee (adviser).


(60)  The role of the Outside Studies Programs Committee will be to:
  1. consider applications from the Schools;
  2. provide recommendations to the Provost to approve applications;
  3. scrutinise and provide feedback on reports on completed OSPs;
  4. oversee and consider matters relating to OSP including the development of rules and standards relating to OSP.


## Part D - Travel and Financial Assistance
### Approval for Overseas Travel
(61)  Approval for an OSP which includes a component of overseas travel is contingent upon University approval to travel to the destinations listed in the application.
(62)  Travel to places where a DFAT warning against travel is in place will not be approved unless a convincing reason is provided to indicate that the travel is essential.
(63)  Applicants whose OSP includes overseas travel should refer to the [OSP How-to Guide](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=233&version=2&associated) and the University's Guide on [Booking and managing travel](https://intranet.latrobe.edu.au/tasks-and-processes/travel-transport-and-parking).
### Financial Assistance
(64)  There are two types of financial assistance that may be available to a staff member travelling on OSP:
  1. a grant may be payable to assist with overseas, interstate, or intrastate travel expenses;
  2. a staff member may be able to claim a salary advance for travel purposes.


#### Financial Grant
(65)  For staff members travelling overseas, interstate or intrastate on OSP, a grant may be payable to assist with expenses. The amount of the grant is the same for full time and part time staff members. For overseas and interstate travel it is based on the length of time to be spent overseas/interstate, with a minimum component of one month. Staff members who receive an overseas grant will not be eligible for an interstate or intrastate grant.
(66)  In addition to the grant payable to staff travelling overseas an allowance for up to three dependents will be paid, subject to evidence that they are travelling with the staff member.
(67)  Financial grants apply only to the period of OSP and not to any long service leave, excess recreation leave or leave without pay taken in conjunction with an OSP.
(68)  For further information on financial grants, including amounts payable, please refer to the [OSP How-to Guide](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=233&version=2&associated).
#### Salary Advance
(69)  A staff member may claim half their normal salary for the period of overseas study in the form of a salary advance for travel purposes, subject to Australian Taxation Office rules. Refer to the [OSP How-to Guide](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=233&version=2&associated) for further information.
(70)  An alternative mechanism for a salary advance is provided in the [La Trobe University Enterprise Agreement 2023](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=422&version=2&associated); with four weeks’ notice, a staff member will be entitled to payment in advance for periods of paid OSP in excess of two (2) weeks up to a maximum of 12 weeks. Enquiries may be directed to People & Culture.
## Part E - Variations to Programs
(71)  Variations to approved programs must be submitted to the OSP administrator in advance.
(72)  The University's online travel booking and leave request systems must not be used to alter a previously approved OSP and associated recreation leave or long service leave.
(73)  Where a staff member requests a postponement of the commencement date for a period not exceeding six months from the commencement date of the approved OSP, and this is approved by the Dean, no further approval will be required.
(74)  Where a postponement is for a period greater than six months from the commencement date of the approved OSP, the staff member must resubmit the application.
(75)  Where a staff member requests a substantial change to a program, full details of the changes must be submitted for the approval of the OSP Chair, through the Dean. Any change which involves the elimination of an overseas component will be automatically regarded as a substantial change.
(76)  Where the Dean or OSP Chair considers that a changed program is of insufficient merit, approval for all or part of the program may be withdrawn by the OSP Committee on the recommendation of the OSP Chair.
(77)  Variations to approved programs involving an extension to, or addition of, an overseas or interstate component may be approved, but normally no further grant will be provided.
## Part F - Unsuccessful Applications
(78)  The decision not to approve an application will be based on the quality/merit of the proposed program and/or on the resources available within the School.
(79)  The OSP Chair will provide unsuccessful applicants with brief written advice outlining the reasons why their applications were not approved.
(80)  Where the decision was based on the quality/merit of the proposed program the letter will include advice on areas that would need to be strengthened before a future application was submitted. The OSP Chair is encouraged to meet with the applicants individually to discuss this further.
(81)  It is suggested that applicants use this advice, in consultation with their supervisor, when revising their workload and performance development plans.
### Appeals
(82)  Applicants will have the right to appeal against the decision in relation to their applications. Appeals can only be made on the grounds that the procedures outlined in this document were not followed by the OSP Committee in reaching its decision.
(83)  An appeal is to be lodged with the Provost via email to OSPC@latrobe.edu.au within one month of the applicant’s receipt of advice on the outcome of the application.
(84)  Any appeal against the decision made by the Provost in relation to an appeal should be made to the University Ombudsman and only on the grounds of failure to follow the procedures pertaining to the submission and consideration of an appeal.
## Part G - Authorities/Delegations
(85)  The OSP Chair is responsible for: 
  1. overseeing the number of programs a school could offer in any one year;
  2. approving programs, with the advice of Deans in consultation with the professor(s) of discipline.


(86)  Reports on completed OSPs:
  1. The OSP Committee will scrutinise and approve reports through the Dean and OSP Chair.

# Section 7 - Definitions
(87)  For the purpose of this Policy and Procedure:
  1. Relative to opportunity: relates to acknowledgement of what a staff member can and has achieved given the workload allocation and opportunities available. Personal circumstances that could affect opportunity may include family responsibilities, a temporary or permanent disability, and periods of part-time work and/or absences due to ill-health or injury.

sections.heading: Section 5 - Policy Statement
sections.text:
(4)  Undertaking Outside Work may have benefits for the individual staff member and the University. The University does not preclude such arrangements from occurring, provided:
  1. the staff member discloses the arrangements to the University;
  2. the arrangements do not interfere with the staff member’s discharge of their professional duties or encroach unduly on work time;
  3. the arrangements do not create a conflict with other obligations that cannot be actively and appropriately managed; and
  4. the proposed activity is not contrary to the University’s interests, values or reputation.


(5)  Consulting delivered through the University by a staff member must be approved and negotiated in accordance with University policies and procedures.

sections.heading: Part A - Outside Work
sections.text:
(6)  Outside Work consists of:
  1. University Consulting which is fee for service work performed by a staff member (full or part-time) through the University for an external organisation or individual, which is over and above their workload allocation and/or University duties/position description; and
  2. Personal Work which is work performed by a full-time staff member in their personal capacity outside their contract of employment with the University.


(7)  All staff members may engage in Outside Work:
  1. up to the paid external work cap, with approval through PRIME by the Dean or Head of Administrative Division; or
  2. above the paid external work cap if the approval has been agreed through PRIME and the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Innovation) or nominee has agreed through PRIME that the outside work does not compromise the interests of the University.


(8)  The paid external work cap is set at, 5 working days in a month or 48 working days in a calendar year.

sections.heading: Non-permissible Outside Work
Approval of Outside Work: Within Paid External Work Cap
sections.text:
(10)  Deans or Heads of Administrative Divisions are responsible for approving Outside Work within the paid external cap limit, if and only if:
  1. they are in possession of a completed record and declaration in PRIME
  2. they are satisfied that the record and declaration in PRIME is true and complete
  3. the outside work does not compromise the interests of the University


(11)  Deans or Heads of Administrative Divisions have the discretion to withhold approval if:
  1. a staff member proposing to undertake outside work fails to lodge a completed PRIME record and declaration in PRIME fourteen (14) days before the work is proposed to commence, unless otherwise agreed and approved; or
  2. they believe that there is a risk that the proposed work may interfere with the staff member’s ability to perform their University duties.


(12)  Deans or Heads of Administrative Divisions may stipulate reasonable conditions as part of any approval in PRIME. They must complete the approvers comments field in PRIME to record any decisions, provide reasons and stipulate any conditions.
(13)  Deans or Heads of Administrative Divisions must communicate any decisions at least seven (7) days before the date on which the work is proposed to commence to the staff member making the proposal through PRIME.
(14)  Reviews and approvals by relevant approvals will be facilitated through PRIME after submission to the Research Office.

sections.heading: Approval of Outside Work: Exceeding Paid External Work Cap
sections.text:
(15)  The approval of the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Innovation), or their nominee is required where the paid external work cap would be exceeded.
(16)  The Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Innovation), or their nominee, may approve proposals to undertake outside work exceeding the, cap if and only if:
  1. the Dean or Head of Administrative Division has provided approval in accordance with these Procedures; and
  2. the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Innovation), or their nominee is satisfied that the proposed outside work is not against the interests of the University.

sections.heading: Compliance with this Policy
sections.text:
(17)  Deans and Heads of Division are responsible for:
  1. ensuring staff in their relevant School or Division comply with the process and requirements outlined in this Policy; and
  2. monitoring the approved Personal Work Records for their relevant School or Division via the reporting functionality available in PRIME.

sections.heading: Part B - University Consulting
Benefits of University Consulting
Consultancy Submission, Costing, Pricing and Approval
sections.text:
(21)  University Consulting proposals should be submitted by staff for approval via PRIME prior to submission to a prospective client.
(22)  All resources required to undertake the proposed project should be identified in the proposal and costed using the budget tool in PRIME or the Consulting Rate Card. 
(23)  Reviews and approvals by relevant approvers will be facilitated through PRIME after submission to the Research Office.
(24)  The School/Division will be responsible for any over-expenditure.
(25)  University consultancies must abide by [Australian Competition and Consumer Law](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/directory/summary.php?legislation=27). See the University’s [Factsheet](https://intranet.latrobe.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0015/306123/ACL-Factsheet.pdf) on Australian Competition and Consumer Law, the University’s [Contracts Policy](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=30), and the [ACCC](https://www.accc.gov.au/) website,for further information.

sections.heading: University Consultancy Agreements
sections.text:
(26)  Any legal conditions must either accord with a University’s standard form Consulting Agreement or be reviewed and approved by the Research Office and/or Legal Services in accordance with the [Contracts Policy](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=30).
(27)  University Consulting Agreements may only be signed by an authorised signatory in accordance with the University’s [Contract Signing Delegations](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=304&version=13&associated).

sections.heading: Consulting Revenue Proceeds
sections.text:
(28)  Revenue for University Consulting must be paid into the University’s bank account and managed in accordance with the University’s financial procedures by the Research Finance Team.
(29)  University Overheads are calculated and distributed by Research Finance to the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Innovation) and to the staff member’s School/Division:
  1. 35% of consulting rates (excluding expenses) distributed as follows: 
    1. 17.5% to the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Innovation); and
    2. 17.5% to the staff members School or Administrative Division.


(30)  After recovery of University Overheads and project expenses, the balance of consulting revenue will be transferred to employees’ nominated outside earnings accounts or paid through payroll (less required taxes and SGC superannuation).
(31)  Any balances of staff outside earning accounts will remain with the University upon termination or departure from the University by the staff member.

sections.heading: Conduct During University Consulting
sections.text:
(32)  Staff members engaged in University Consulting must not:
  1. use the University’s resources or intellectual property to benefit a third party without University approval by the Dean or head of Administrative Division;
  2. take any action or make any statement as part of their University Consulting which may serve to bring the University into disrepute by association; and
  3. allow their private interests or the interests of others to interfere or be perceived to interfere with their obligation to act in the best interest of the University.


(33)  It is a condition of approval that the employee confirms that they remains bound by all University policies with respect to conduct, particularly the [Code of Conduct](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=71), while performing the University Consulting.

sections.heading: Declaration of Proposed Personal Work
sections.text:
(34)  Full-time staff members proposing to engage in any Personal Work, whether for payment or not, must submit a completed personal work record and declaration in PRIME for approval by their Dean or Head of Administrative Division at least fourteen (14) days before the personal work is proposed to commence or sooner by agreement with approval.
(35)  Certain Personal Work is deemed to be automatically approved unless a real, potential or perceived conflict of interest exists as follows:
  1. work where there is no connection or association with the employee’s University duties, the work is undertaken outside of normal University hours of work and does not adversely impact on or create a conflict of interest with their University duties;
  2. directorships of for-purpose organisations, or organisations formed to deal solely with private affairs;
  3. advice to parliamentary committees, tribunals and other public bodies; and
  4. support, organisation and administration for professional bodies directly linked to the staff member’s role or professional disciplinary conferences.


(36)  Staff members (full-time or part-time) engaged in Personal Work must:
  1. manage any possible conflict of interest, and intellectual property and foreign interference following the [Conflict of Interest Policy](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=83), and [Intellectual Property Statute 2009](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/directory/summary.php?legislation=70), [Foreign Influence](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/directory/summary.php?legislation=143), and the associated policy and procedures;
  2. ensure the work does not inhibit or detract from the standards of performance of duties for the University; and
  3. advise third parties for whom such work is undertaken that it is not being undertaken on behalf of the University.


(37)  If Personal Work is undertaken:
  1. such work is not covered by any University insurances. The staff member must maintain adequate insurance coverage including professional indemnity and public liability coverage in relation to the work; and
  2. the financial proceeds must not be deposited into University accounts.

The University does have a [Paid Additional Work Within the University - Full Time Staff Procedure](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=53).

sections.heading: Part D - Complaints and Breach of this Policy
sections.text:
(42)  Staff should refer to the [Enterprise Agreement](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=422&version=2&associated) or their contract of employment with respect to complaints pertaining to conditions of Outside Work. The complaint should be progressed in accordance with the [Workplace Issue Resolution (Staff) Procedure](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/document/view.php?id=51) as per [La Trobe University Enterprise Agreement 2023](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=422&version=2&associated).
(43)  A breach of this Policy may be dealt with by the relevant approver by:
  1. reviewing the approval for the Outside Work and amending or withdrawing approval;
  2. referring the matter as per [La Trobe University Enterprise Agreement 2023](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=422&version=2&associated) to consider whether action should be taken; and
  3. any other action considered necessary by the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research and Innovation), or their nominee.

sections.heading: Section 7 - Definitions
sections.text:
(44)  For the purpose of this Policy and Procedure:
  1. Foreign Arrangement Scheme is the scheme created by Australia’s [Foreign Relations (State and Territory) Act 2020](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/directory/summary.php?legislation=148) (“the Act”) to ensure Australian entities do not adversely affect Australia’s foreign relations and are not inconsistent with Australia’s foreign policy. The Act requires the University to notify the Minister of Foreign Affairs of all arrangements that the University has and proposes to enter with foreign entities. Further information and guidance is available [here](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=333&version=5&associated).
  2. Foreign Influence: Activities carried out by or on behalf of a foreign actor conducted in an open and transparent manner, are a normal aspect of international relations and diplomacy and can contribute positively to public debate. Further information and guidance is available [here](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=333&version=5&associated).
  3. Foreign Interference: Activities carried out by, or on behalf of, a foreign actor, which are coercive, covert, deceptive or corrupting and are contrary to Australia’s sovereignty, values and national interests. Further information and guidance is available [here](https://policies.latrobe.edu.au/download.php?id=333&version=5&associated).
  4. Outside Work: means work undertaken not for the University or as part of the normal duties of the employee’s role and includes employment or any other form of paid work external to the University, including proprietorship, directorships, independent contracting, or consultancy.
  5. Personal Work: is work performed by a full-time staff member in their personal capacity outside their contract of employment with the University.
  6. PRIME: the University’s platform to manage the development, approvals and management of Research Grants, Collaborations and Consulting proposals and projects including non-research consulting, ethics and personal work processes. You can access PRIME here: <https://prime.latrobe.edu.au/portal/s/>
  7. University Consulting: fee-for-service work performed by an employee through La Trobe where net revenue is to be transferred to an outside earnings account, or paid into salary. Consulting is over and above an employee’s workload allocation and/or University duties unless otherwise agreed, and does not include Research or the development or delivery of subjects and courses both award or non-award.
  8. University Overheads: costs that are related to the day-to-day running of the University, which typically includes costs associated with the use of facilities (for example lights, power, telephone, computer and certain equipment), administrative support, legal costs, insurance costs, project administration, audit and financial management costs.
